summary.text: Lois Frankel is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for the 23rd District, first elected to the House in 2012 and now in her seventh term. A lawyer by training, she previously served in the Florida House of Representatives, including as minority leader, and as mayor of West Palm Beach. She sits on the House Appropriations Committee and is running for re-election.

paragraphs.text: Frankel was born in New York, New York, in 1948. She earned a bachelor's degree in psychology from Boston University in 1970 and a J.D. from Georgetown University in 1973.
She worked as a lawyer before holding elective office.
She served in the Florida House of Representatives from 1986 to 1992 and again from 1994 to 2002, including as minority leader from 2000 to 2002.
Frankel served as mayor of West Palm Beach from 2003 to 2011.
She won the Democratic nomination and the November 6, 2012 general election for the U.S. House and took office in 2013; her official site describes her as in her seventh term.

She is a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, where she is the lead Democrat on the Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs and also serves on the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Subcommittee.
According to her official site, Frankel is Chair Emerita of the Democratic Women's Caucus and Co-Chair of the bipartisan Women, Peace, and Security Caucus.
Her official biography describes her as an avid abstract painter, the mother of a U.S. Marine veteran, and a grandmother of two.
She won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 74.8% of the vote over Victoria Doyle and Mark Piper.
